stem: Calls arrive at a helpdesk at an average rate of 3 calls per hour. Assuming a Poisson distribution, what is the probability of receiving exactly 0 calls in a given hour? [Given: e^(-3) = 0.0498]

per_option_rationale.rationale: 0.1494 = 3*e^(-3) = P(X=1); the student computed one success term lambda^1/1! = 3*0.0498 instead of P(X=0).
0.9502 = 1 - e^(-3) = 1 - 0.0498; the student computed P(X>=1) (the complement of zero) instead of P(X=0).
0.0166 = e^(-3)/3 = 0.0498/3; the student divided e^(-lambda) by lambda rather than multiplying by lambda^0/0!=1.

explanation: Poisson formula: P(X=k) = e^(-lambda)*lambda^k/k!. For k=0: lambda^0=1, 0!=1, so P(X=0)=e^(-3)=0.0498.

explanation_sections.punchline: P(X=0) in the Poisson distribution equals e^(-lambda) directly, since lambda^0=1 and 0!=1.
explanation_sections.approach: Model: Poisson(lambda=3). Map: k=0. Formula: P(X=0)=e^(-3)*3^0/0!=e^(-3)=0.0498. Use the given hint.
explanation_sections.lesson: Poisson P(X=0) = e^(-lambda); memorise this as a one-line special case.
explanation_sections.timing: 30 seconds. Direct read-off from the hint; no arithmetic needed. Trap: multiplying by lambda.
